data.generation: Euler-Maruyama at dt_fine = 0.01 for the Day 7 ground-truth Geometric SDE (see ground_truth_sde). Observations every 0.05 on [0, 10] (201 points per trajectory). Initial states are lognormal: X^1(0) ~ LogNormal(log 2, 0.4), X^2(0) ~ LogNormal(0, 0.4), independent per trajectory, so every trajectory starts strictly positive (the GSDE domain).
data.thinning: For teacher training only, each train trajectory's interior observations are dropped independently with probability 0.5 (seed 123, first and last observations always kept), mimicking the paper's 50% missing-rate regime (paper Figure 1 uses a 50% missing rate). Transitions for the thinned teachers join consecutive kept observations with dt = gap * 0.05 (variable-dt EM). Field queries, SINDy queries, and all test evaluations use the full regular grid, so training missingness is the distribution shift under test.

distillation.diffusion_library_variables: Per-component GSDE libraries: g^1 is fitted on polynomials in (t, X^1) only, g^2 on polynomials in (t, X^2) only. The paper's GSDE diffusion is g^j = X^j * sigma^j(t): each component's diffusion depends on its own state and on t, never on the other component. A full-library (t, X^1, X^2) diffusion fit is reported as a diagnostic for spurious cross-dependence (Day 6 reflection: diffusion inputs verified separately from drift).
distillation.diffusion_targets: per-dimension diffusion levels g^1, g^2 (diagonal diffusion). Headline diffusion error is the joint NRMSE over (g^1, g^2); implied Sigma = diag(g^2) NRMSE is reported separately because Sigma is the identified object.
distillation.drift_library_variables: polynomials in (X^1, X^2) only (no t). The truth is time-homogeneous, so a t-free library tests whether the teacher's t-dependence is negligible; teacher t-variation at fixed states is reported as a separate diagnostic.
distillation.oracle_diagnostic: the same SINDy procedure fitted to ground-truth field values at the same query states (diagnostic ceiling only, not a candidate)
distillation.query_states: observed states of each split (trajectory-disjoint train/validation/test), teacher evaluated directly (no finite differences)
distillation.selection: per field, minimize validation NRMSE against the teacher; test evaluated once after selection

ground_truth_sde.diffusion: g^1 = 0.30 * X^1, g^2 = 0.25 * X^2 (diagonal, one independent Brownian motion per component). In the paper's GSDE form dz/z = gamma dt + sigma dW, this is sigma^1 = 0.30, sigma^2 = 0.25 constant.
ground_truth_sde.drift: f^1 = X^1 * (0.60 - 0.25 X^1 - 0.10 X^2), f^2 = X^2 * (-0.10 + 0.20 X^1 - 0.30 X^2). In the paper's GSDE form, gamma^1 = 0.60 - 0.25 X^1 - 0.10 X^2 and gamma^2 = -0.10 + 0.20 X^1 - 0.30 X^2 (linear gamma, hence exactly quadratic effective drift). The interior equilibrium is (X^1, X^2) = (2, 1) with Jacobian [[-0.5, -0.2], [0.2, -0.3]] (stable spiral).
ground_truth_sde.form: Geometric SDE (paper Eq. (6)): dZ/Z = gamma(t, Z) dt + sigma(t) dW, i.e. in Ito form dZ = Z * gamma dt + Z * sigma dW, componentwise. The truth used here is the time-homogeneous, constant-sigma special case with linear gamma, chosen so that the effective drift is exactly polynomial (degree 2) and the effective diffusion exactly linear, making coefficient recovery a meaningful question (unlike Day 6's tanh truth).

H2_diffusion_distillation.note: Headline is the (g^1, g^2) joint NRMSE; the Sigma clause is the identified-object clause. Both must hold.

H3_truth_recovery.note: Field-level clause. Coefficient clause H3c is reported separately (see below) and does not gate H3, per the Day 1 lesson that field and coefficient verdicts must be separated.

H3c_linear_coefficients.note: Linear-coefficient clause only, because the collinearity gate (VIF 1.05 for the linear variables, but 16-26 for the degree-2 library on prototype queries) supports linear coefficients and not quadratic ones. Compared quantities: the expanded symbolic coefficients of X^1 and X^2 in f^1 (truth 0.60, 0.00) and in f^2 (truth 0.00, -0.10). Quadratic coefficients (truth f^1: X^1^2 -0.25, X^1 X^2 -0.10, X^2^2 0.00; f^2: X^1^2 0.00, X^1 X^2 0.20, X^2^2 -0.30) are tabulated without a pass/fail verdict.

H4_simulation.domain_excursion_definition: fraction of simulated trajectories whose radius sqrt((X^1)^2 + (X^2)^2) ever exceeds 8.0 (above the largest radius seen in the scale prototype, ~6.9) at any simulated step; a domain-validity measure separate from failure (Day 4 reflection). Negativity (any X^j < 0) is counted as a second, GSDE-specific domain measure.
H4_simulation.note: Paired RMSE is the per-step 2D Euclidean distance between symbolic and teacher simulated states, median over test trajectories and steps. The threshold is set from the state scale (equilibrium radius ~2.24, component stds ~0.55/0.35 in the prototype). Failure is non-finite state or radius > 30.

coarse_step_negativity.note: Paired simulation at dt = 0.5 (20 steps, T = 10) from test initial states with shared increments: the paper's Euler-instability axis (Section 2.2). Clause: negativity rate (naive-thinned minus GSDE-thinned) > 0 and > 2 x paired SE of the per-trajectory binary difference.

drift_degradation.note: Degradation = mean squared drift error vs truth on test queries for the thinned teacher minus that for the dense teacher, per teacher class. Clause: degradation(naive) - degradation(GSDE) > 0 and > 2 x paired SE, where the SE is from per-query paired differences of squared errors. Both the degradation clause and the negativity clause must hold.
drift_degradation.paired_se_rule: mean difference > 0 and > 2 x paired SE (same rule as Day 6 H5, no fixed absolute margin)

H6_discretization_bias_em_coarsening.coarsening: GSDE-structured EM teacher retrained on observations subsampled to Delta t = 0.5 (every 10th observation) vs GSDE-structured EM teacher trained on the same number of transitions subsampled from Delta t = 0.05 data (transition-count-matched, Day 6 lesson).
H6_discretization_bias_em_coarsening.note: Day 1 reflection adapted to GSDEs, with Day 6's regime lesson: the hypothesis is regime-split by state radius, because freezing bias for a multiplicative system grows with state magnitude. Small regime = radius < 2 (43.6% of prototype queries), large regime = radius > 3 (8.1%), middle band excluded.

H7_downstream_one_step.note: |MSE_symbolic - MSE_teacher| for one-step-ahead X^1 predictions on regular test transitions, using realized next states. Paired SE reported; if paired SE >= 0.0025 (half the threshold) the clause is reported as 'not statistically established' even if the point estimate passes (Day 4 reflection).

paper.authors: YongKyung Oh, Dong-Young Lim, Sungil Kim
paper.experiment: Sections 3-4: three stable Neural SDE classes (Langevin-type LSDE Eq. (4), Linear Noise LNSDE Eq. (5), Geometric GSDE Eq. (6)) for irregular time series, with controlled-path drift augmentation (Eq. (10)) and robustness theorems under distribution shift from missing data (Theorems 3.5-3.6). Experiments on PhysioNet Mortality/Sepsis, Speech Commands, and MuJoCo at several missing rates; Figure 1 shows naive diffusion choices (e.g. |z|^3, free neural g) destabilizing training at 50% missing rate. Proposition 3.4(ii): GSDE solutions stay nonnegative a.s. with 0 absorbing.
paper.title: Stable Neural Stochastic Differential Equations in Analyzing Irregular Time Series Data

reflections_applied.day1_collinearity_gate: Before fitting, corr and VIF are computed on train query states for both the linear variables (VIF 1.05 on prototype) and the degree-2 library (VIF 16-26). The coefficient hypothesis is therefore restricted to linear coefficients (H3c); quadratic coefficients are tabulated without a verdict, and large high-degree coefficients are read as cancellation / off-manifold risk, not mechanism (Day 4).
reflections_applied.day1_discretization_bias: H6 is the adapted discretization-bias diagnostic: GSDE-structured EM at Delta t = 0.05 (transition-count-matched) vs Delta t = 0.5, with the degradation split by state-radius regimes (small < 2 vs large > 3) instead of tanh regimes, because the GSDE truth has no saturating activation. Drift and Sigma errors are reported with absolute RMS alongside NRMSE.
reflections_applied.day2_off_manifold: Off-manifold diagnostic is standard: a fixed grid over the positive quadrant (including the near-zero corner x < 0.5, y < 0.5, outside the typical data range) at t = 5, reported on field / off-manifold axes separately and used for reporting only, never for selection (Day 5 reflection). Where the grid overlaps the data range, no strong extrapolation claim is made (Day 3 reflection).
reflections_applied.day3_diffusion_tie_zone: No estimator ordering is judged on a single g point comparison; diffusion clauses use joint g and Sigma NRMSE with the Day 6 tie-zone logic retained as a diagnostic note for EM-vs-two-stage style comparisons (not applicable: all Day 7 teachers are EM).
reflections_applied.day4_domain_validity: H4 carries two domain clauses separate from failure: radius excursion (> 8) and negativity (any component < 0), the latter being the GSDE-specific domain (Proposition 3.4(ii)).
reflections_applied.day4_downstream_paired_se: H7 reports the paired SE of the one-step MSE difference and marks the clause indeterminate if the paired SE is comparable to the threshold.
reflections_applied.day4_high_order_cancellation: Degree-3 symbolic coefficients, if selected, are read as manifold-cancellation / off-manifold blow-up risk and checked against the grid diagnostic.
reflections_applied.day5_distribution_vs_field: No distribution-matching teacher is used (all teachers are transition-likelihood EM), so no distribution-loss verdict can be confused with a field verdict; teacher-vs-truth and symbolic-vs-teacher errors are tabulated side by side.
reflections_applied.day5_multiple_initial_conditions: Every trajectory has its own lognormal initial state (no single initial condition), by design.
reflections_applied.day5_off_manifold_denominator: Grid NRMSE values above 1 are reported with absolute RMS errors alongside.
reflections_applied.day6_diffusion_input_design: Diffusion is fitted per component on (t, own state) only, reflecting the GSDE structure g^j = X^j sigma^j(t); a full-library (t, X^1, X^2) diffusion fit is reported as a diagnostic for spurious cross-dependence, so a trajectory-constant-input failure mode of the Day 6 type would be visible as cross terms rather than hidden in a joint fit.
reflections_applied.day6_shuffled_lag_analogue: The GSDE analogue of the shuffled-lag diagnostic is the near-zero-corner grid evaluation: the multiplicative structure g^j -> 0 as X^j -> 0 is exactly what fails if a polynomial fit invents cross-dependence or a nonzero intercept, so the corner subset is reported separately.
reflections_applied.day6_term_readability: The truth is low-degree, so the symbolic model is expected to be sparse; the report summarizes the linear part and term counts and puts the full TeX expansion in the outputs file (the Day 6 375-term lesson in reverse: sparsity here is itself a finding).

simulation.negativity_definition: any simulated component < 0 at any step (GSDE domain measure, Proposition 3.4(ii))

teacher.architecture: GSDE-structured teacher: gamma net MLP [32, 32] tanh on (t, X^1, X^2) with output 1.5 * tanh(raw) per component (bounded gamma, paper Assumption 3.2 / Proposition 3.4(ii) tanh last layer); sigma net MLP [16] tanh on t only, output softplus(raw) + 0.01 per component; effective drift f^j = X^j * gamma^j, effective diffusion g^j = X^j * sigma^j(t) (diagonal, one independent Brownian motion per component). Naive teacher: free MLP [32, 32] tanh on (t, X^1, X^2) for drift, and a second free MLP [32, 32] tanh for diffusion levels g = softplus(raw) + 0.01 (no multiplicative structure, no t-only restriction). Inputs standardized with train statistics (train only). A variance floor of 1e-8 is added to the EM variance to keep the NLL finite where X^j is small.
teacher.deviation_from_paper: Four declared cuts. (1) Latent classification task replaced by an identifiable observable GSDE: the paper's GSDE is a latent representation for classification/interpolation on PhysioNet/Speech data, whose latent coordinates are not identifiable; following the charter, the teacher is reconstructed in identifiable coordinates as an observable 2D GSDE with linear gamma and constant sigma, instead of the paper's latent + classifier + controlled-path pipeline. The controlled path (Eq. (10)), the classifier head, and the PhysioNet/Speech/MuJoCo benchmarks are not treated. (2) Training is by Euler-Maruyama Gaussian transition likelihood (variable dt for thinned data) rather than the paper's solver-based training through the latent pipeline; this is the series' standard estimator and is declared as a method substitution, not as the paper's training. (3) Only the GSDE class is treated (LSDE and LNSDE are not); the paper's three-class comparison is reduced to GSDE vs naive free-MLP, which is the paper's own Figure 1 contrast (stable class vs naive diffusion). (4) The missing-rate shift is implemented as observation thinning (50%) on synthetic trajectories rather than real missing-data benchmarks; the paper's missing-rate robustness claim is therefore tested only in its synthetic analogue, not on the paper's datasets.

em_coarse.transitions: train trajectories subsampled to every 10th observation (640 x 20 = 12800 transitions)

em_fine_sub.transitions: 12800 transitions subsampled at random (seed-fixed) from train Delta t = 0.05 transitions, matching the coarsened count

teacher.estimator: em (Euler-Maruyama Gaussian transition likelihood, variable dt for thinned transitions)

estimators_compared.em_gsde_dense: GSDE-structured EM on full regular train transitions (dt = 0.05)
estimators_compared.em_gsde_thinned: GSDE-structured EM on 50%-thinned train transitions (variable dt) -- the distilled teacher, fixed a priori because the paper's setting is irregular (missing) data
estimators_compared.em_naive_dense: naive free-MLP EM on full regular train transitions
estimators_compared.em_naive_thinned: naive free-MLP EM on 50%-thinned train transitions (variable dt)
